text: So I think about having spent / ninety-nine years on the Earth.
Now I’m on my deathbed. I can’t move much.
And I feel the grim reaper approaching.
Life comes to an end for all of us.
We cannot stop that time from coming.
We are not immortal, as far as I’m aware.
So I think about all the time I spent / nurturing and caring for my emotional needs—
an emotional family, personified—
the health and well-being of my brain and body.
In my mind’s eye, I see them.
Their hands on my shoulders. My arms. My legs.
They run their hands through what hair I have left.
With love and care, a knowing look: / I cared for them while I could care for them.
I protected them while I could protect them.
Now that I can’t protect them all that much anymore, / they still want to protect me.
They are going to care for me in my last moments.
Instead of the reaper, / they are the first thing on my mind—
them, and the love I sought to cultivate / for humanity as a whole,
and my own life, / as the curtain to the show of life closes.
The reaper was the last thing on my mind / while I was with them.
The closer I am to death / doesn’t mean I let death take me.
It means the harder I hold on / to all the love that was grown in the garden of life.
Because I don’t want to lose it— / when I die, this experience I had living in the universe dies.
So the reaper is going to have to / drag my ass out of there—
and I’m not going to go easy. 😉
You might say I fear death— / but it doesn’t control my life.
I don’t want to run away and hide. / I want to run to my emotional family,
to hug them, and tell them before death gets here: / I am here for you.
You will be in my heart forever, not death.
Death is on the outside.
Even if death comes, I am here for you— / right now, and forever, until my last breath.
In my daily life, I see their emotional needs, / and I speak with them as a human—
because I am human, / and they are a part of our shared humanity.
I treat them with a kind of prohuman / introspective respect.
They deserve all the respect I deserve. / Because they are me.
They help me navigate the world / toward more well-being, less suffering.
Through the ebbs and flows of life, / they are in the ship with me.
I carry them as they carry me.
They hug me, and they close their eyes. / I close my eyes. We hug each other closer.
I feel at one with them, and they with me— / because they were me the whole time.
They were with me the whole time, / and I was with them the whole time.
Unity isn’t to silence or dismiss my emotions. / It’s the culmination of all my life with them,
because they were my life— / because they were me.
I want to hold them, and I need them to hold me too, / so I can feel safer in this world.
We were together from the day we were born, / and we will be together until the end.
When they die, I die.
But when I live for them, I live for myself.
And when they live for me, I feel love—
and I want to love them.
